chapter: Carnegie Hall, nicknames and later career
title: First time at Carnegie Hall with Benny Goodman, and Marian Anderson
summary: Basie recalls his 1938 Carnegie debut on 'Honeysuckle Rose' with Goodman, and hearing Marian Anderson there with Hammond.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Do you remember the first time you were in Carnegie Hall?
No? Do you remember the time you were at Carnegie Hall with Benny?
Tell me about 1938 when you were with Benny Goodman at Carnegie. It says here that was the first time you played Carnegie, I think. What do you remember of that?

Well, I can remember that -- well, I know it was a Benny Goodman concert, and it was like the first jazz concert that I heard in Carnegie and was the one I had the pleasure of being a part of it. I did a thing with Benny then on "Honeysuckle Rose."
Yes, I remember it very well. It was a great concert, and that was my first time at Carnegie Hall onstage. John had once taken me to hear Marion Anderson, which is something I will never forget.
Because she was just such a wonderful lady. Such a great singer. And I didn't know when I first went with John if I was going to be able to actually dig her.
and she really upset me. She was so marvelous.
Yeah, I know that was the first time I had ever been on the stage at Carnegie Hall.
Could your band ever have played for Marion Anderson?
I don't think we could. She was just such a serious singer, you know. She was in a whole different thing. (UNINTELLIGIBLE) [It was a different department altogether]

And I had one of the greatest experiences of my life... And I cut a side with her ... but she was one of the all-time great singers and I'm not gonna tell you was such a great person. It was called (unintelligible) the name.
I guess I've never heard it.

Oh, you've heard it. But that was a great time, the concert with Bennie, and the thrill of just being and working at Carnegie Hall -- it sort of gave you goose pimples, you know. (Inaudible) My fingers were kinda damp when I started to play.
